definition: Information search may refer to: use of a Search engine (tool centered view) Information seeking or Information behavior (user centered view) Information retrieval (technical process)
details: Information search may refer to: use of a Search engine (tool centered view) Information seeking or Information behavior (user centered view) Information retrieval (technical process)

explainer.lead: Information search is an umbrella term covering use of a search engine, information seeking behavior, and the technical retrieval process. It matters as a label that spans tool-centred, user-centred and technical views.

tiers.eli5: Searching for information can mean using the search box, the human habit of hunting for answers, or the machinery underneath—three views of one activity.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers should be explicit about which view they mean, since a tool-centred search feature is not the same as modeling user information behavior. The pitfall is conflating these levels when designing or evaluating systems.
tiers.paperLevel: Information search may refer to: use of a search engine (tool-centred view), information seeking or information behavior (user-centred view), or information retrieval (technical process).

explainer.example: A product team building a search box (tool view) also studies how users hunt for answers (behavior view) and how the retrieval system ranks results (technical view).
